newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end a notch higher on company results.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end a notch higher on company results.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange chalked up further moderate gains Friday, spurred by strong quarterly company results in the mining sector, but brokers noted volumes were thin.

"The (company) results confirm that industry is in the process of recovering from the hammering it suffered last year and mining and public sector companies did particulary well," said analyst Victor Bernardo Asto at brokerage Finvest.
The blue-chip index .ISEL closed up 0.38 percent at 2,575.97 points, while the general index .IGRA ended up 0.16 percent at 1,761.62.

Traders said the low volume of 18.6 million soles ($7 million) of shares traded was due to market players' already having anticipated the good company results and therefore having already picked up stocks in these companies.
Brokers expected investors to return to the market next week to pick up stocks with good long-term prospects.

Most market attention was on mining company Perubar which rallied to close up 5.19 percent to 4.05 soles, with 78,567 shares traded, and Morococha which rallied to close up 9.92 percent at 2.77 soles, with 247,270 shares traded.

Shares in electrical company Edegel closed up 0.77 percent to 1.31 soles, with 611,443 shares traded, and telecom company Telefonica del Peru "B" closed up 0.31 percent at 6.44 soles, with 513,386 shares.
On the downside, shares in D'Onofrio fell 3.25 percent to 1.19 soles, with 63,447 shares traded.
Holding Credicorp fell 0.29 percent to $20.98, with 15,896 shares traded and miner Minsur shed 0.27 percent to 10.94 soles with 80,372 share traded.
Electronic firm Edelnor ended down 1.74 percent at 2.26 soles, with 33,174 shares traded, and Luz del Sur lost 0.63 percent to close at 3.15 soles, with 168,554 shares traded.
"The price of various shares are well placed, but after results are out, market players are likely to revise their positions," said trader Luis Calderon at brokerage Acciones y Valores.

Peru's dominant brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas SA, which was formed in December 1996, from four breweries -- Backus y Johnston, Compania Nacional de Cerveza, Sociedad Cervecera de Trujillo SA and Cerveceria del Norte -- beloning to the Backus group, will start trading on the Lima Stock Exchange with a single listing.
